title: Crystal Hefner Urges Jessica Biel to Skip Role as Hugh Hefner’s Wife in Upcoming Film—TMZ Report
body:
Crystal Hefner, the former wife of Playboy magnate Hugh Hefner, has publicly appealed to actress Jessica Biel to reconsider accepting a role that would cast her as the legendary publisher’s spouse in an upcoming biographical film. Hefner, who has become an outspoken critic of the way Hugh Hefner’s legacy is portrayed in popular culture, warned Biel that the project could romanticize a figure and an era that many view as exploitative and out of step with contemporary values.

The proposed picture, currently untitled, is being developed by a major studio that aims to chart the rise of Playboy from its modest beginnings in a Chicago apartment to its status as a global brand. Biel, known for her work in both television dramas and blockbuster films, was reportedly approached last month to portray Crystal in scenes that would span the 1970s and 1980s, a period marked by the magazine’s cultural dominance and its founder’s flamboyant lifestyle. While the studio has not released a full casting list, insiders confirm that the script depicts Hugh Hefner as a visionary entrepreneur, emphasizing his role in shaping sexual liberation and media innovation.

Crystal Hefner’s objections are rooted in personal experience and a broader cultural reassessment of the Playboy empire. In a heartfelt Instagram post, she recounted the “dark side” of the lifestyle she once shared with her late husband, describing how the brand’s emphasis on objectifying women left lasting emotional scars. “I’m not trying to silence history,” she wrote, “but I’m asking Jessica to think about the message she’s sending when she steps into a role that could glorify a man who profited from women’s bodies.” Her comments echo a growing chorus of former Playmates, feminist activists, and scholars who argue that Playboy’s legacy is inseparable from the exploitation and commodification of female sexuality.

Industry analysts see Hefner’s public plea as part of a larger trend in Hollywood where biopics are being scrutinized for their moral framing. Recent controversies surrounding films about controversial figures—such as the debates over portrayals of Harvey Weinstein and R. Kelly—have prompted studios to weigh artistic freedom against potential backlash. “Studios are increasingly aware that casting decisions and narrative tone can ignite public discourse,” said media consultant Laura Mendoza. “If the film leans into a nostalgic, celebratory view of Hefner, it risks alienating audiences who are more critical of the patriarchal structures he embodied.”

The studio behind the project has yet to comment on Hefner’s statements, but a spokesperson indicated that the film intends to present a “balanced” view of Hugh Hefner’s impact, acknowledging both his contributions to media and the controversies surrounding his business model. The script reportedly includes scenes that address the magazine’s legal battles, its role in the sexual revolution, and the personal toll it took on those close to Hefner. Whether Biel will remain attached to the role remains uncertain; sources close to the actress say she is “thoughtful” about the responsibility of portraying a real person with a complex legacy.

As the conversation unfolds, the debate highlights the evolving standards by which Hollywood examines historical figures. If the film proceeds with a nuanced narrative, it could serve as a platform for a more critical examination of Playboy’s place in American culture. Conversely, a portrayal that glosses over the ethical concerns raised by Crystal Hefner and others may spark renewed protests and calls for accountability. The outcome will likely influence how future biopics handle contentious subjects, shaping both artistic choices and audience expectations.
